title: Cloud Migration and Compute Terms

header.html: 4. Modernize infrastructure and applications with Google Cloud (about 18%)

4.1 Describe how Google Cloud helps organizations transition to the cloud: define fundamental cloud migration terms (workload, discovery and assessment, retire, retain, rehost, replatform, refactor, reimagine) and fundamental cloud compute terms (virtual machines, containers, microservices, serverless, spot VMs, Kubernetes, autoscaling, load balancing, managed services)
the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide

html:
1Migration terms

A workload is an application or task and the resources it uses. Each workload may take a different path.

Path Meaning Effort and benefit
Discovery and assessment Inventory workloads and decide the path for each First step
Retire Switch off an application that is no longer needed Saves cost
Retain Keep it where it is, for now No change, revisit later
Rehost (lift and shift) Move as is to virtual machines in the cloud Fast, low effort, few cloud benefits
Replatform (move and improve) Move with small changes to use managed services (for example a managed database) Moderate effort, better operations
Refactor Change the code to be cloud-native (for example microservices) High effort, high benefit
Reimagine Rebuild or replace the application to create new business value (new product, AI) Highest effort and innovation
Exam tip

. Rehost = fastest. Refactor and reimagine = most benefit, most effort. Rehost fits specialized legacy apps you cannot change.

2Compute terms

Term Meaning
Virtual machine (VM) A computer simulated in software, with its own operating system
Containerization and containers Packaging an app with what it needs to run the same way anywhere; lighter than VMs
Microservices An app built from small, independent services that scale and update separately
Serverless computing You run code or containers without managing servers; pay per use; scales to zero
Spot VMs Discounted VMs that Google can stop when it needs the capacity; for flexible, fault-tolerant jobs
Kubernetes Open source system to run and manage containers at scale
Autoscaling Add or remove capacity automatically with demand
Load balancing Spread traffic across several servers
Managed services Google runs the operations (patching, scaling, backups) so your team builds instead of operates
Exam tip

. Spot VMs are cheap but can be interrupted, so use them for batch and fault-tolerant work, not for a critical single server.

3How compute options compare

Option Control Management effort
Virtual machines Most Highest
Containers on Kubernetes High Medium
Serverless Least Lowest
Exam tip

. Match the path to the goal: speed = rehost, managed services with small change = replatform, cloud-native benefits = refactor, new business value = reimagine, no longer needed = retire.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A company wants to move a specialized legacy application to the cloud quickly without changing the code. Which migration path fits?

  • AReimagine, which rebuilds the application
  • BRefactor, which rewrites the code
  • CRehost, which moves it as it is
  • DRetire, which switches it off
Show the answer

Answer: C. Rehost, or lift and shift, moves the application as it is, which is fast and needs no code change.

S2A company keeps its database but moves it to a managed database service to cut operations work, with small changes. Which path is this?

  • ARetain, which leaves the application unchanged
  • BRetire, which removes the application completely
  • CReplatform, which makes small changes to use managed services
  • DReimagine, which builds a new product
Show the answer

Answer: C. Replatform, or move and improve, adopts managed services with small changes.

S3An application is no longer used by anyone. What should the assessment recommend?

  • ARehost it to a larger virtual machine
  • BRefactor it into microservices
  • CRetire it to save cost
  • DReimagine it as an AI product
Show the answer

Answer: C. An unused application should be retired.

S4Which step should come first in a migration program?

  • ARefactor every application at once
  • BSwitch off the on-premises data center at the start
  • CDiscovery and assessment of the workloads
  • DBuy more hardware for the old site
Show the answer

Answer: C. Discovery and assessment inventories workloads and chooses a path for each.

S5A company runs nightly batch jobs that can restart if interrupted and wants the lowest compute cost. Which option fits?

  • ASpot VMs, discounted capacity that can be stopped
  • BA single always-on dedicated server
  • CAn on-premises server in a closed room
  • DA manual process run by staff
Show the answer

Answer: A. Spot VMs are discounted and fit fault-tolerant, restartable work.

S6Which technology lets a team run code without managing servers and pay only when it runs?

  • AA dedicated virtual machine
  • BServerless computing
  • CA physical rack of servers
  • DA private fiber connection
Show the answer

Answer: B. Serverless computing removes server management and charges per use.

4.2 Recall questions

R1What does rehost mean?

Show the answer

Move an application as it is (lift and shift).

R2What does refactor mean?

Show the answer

Change the code to be cloud-native.

R3What is a container?

Show the answer

An app packaged with what it needs to run anywhere.

R4What is Kubernetes?

Show the answer

An open source system for running containers at scale.

R5What is a spot VM?

Show the answer

A discounted VM that can be stopped when Google needs capacity.

R6What does autoscaling do?

Show the answer

Adds or removes capacity automatically.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Paths assess, retire, retain, rehost, replatform, refactor, reimagine
Effort rehost least; refactor and reimagine most; benefit rises with effort
Compute VM, container, microservice, serverless, Kubernetes
Cost and scale spot VMs cheap but interruptible; autoscaling; load balancing
